headline: Recount of votes on Question 2, the school district tax and administrative cost cap.
summary: Registered voters asked for the recount after unofficial results showed Question 2 just short of the three-fifths majority needed to pass. If adopted, the question would limit school district property tax growth and SAU central office spending.
items: Recount of votes on Question 2 from the November 3, 2026 election
Adopt the procedures for the recount
Motion to certify the results of the Question 2 recount
location: Manchester SAU Welcome Center, 148 Concord Street, Manchester (Auditorium)

AGENDA  
 
BOARD OF SCHOOL COMMITTEE  
(AS THE BOARD OF RECOUNT) 
RECOUNT OF VOTES CAST REGARDING QUESTION #2 
MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
 
November 20, 2026 8:00 a.m.  
Mayor and all School Board Members Manchester SAU  Welcome Center  
 148 Concord Street, Manchester (Auditorium)  
 
1. Mayor Ruais calls the meeting to order.  
 
2. Mayor Ruais calls for the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
3. The Clerk calls the roll.  
 
4. Mayor Ruais advises that the purpose of this meeting is to recount the votes casts regarding 
question #2 on the November 3rd, 2026 Ballot and requests that a motion be made to adopt the 
procedures for the recounts.   
 
5. Mayor Ruais requests that the Board Clerk begin the process for recount of votes cast on 
Question 2.  
 
6.   Board Clerk Angela Carey makes a brief presentation.  We will now begin the recount 
process. 
 
7. The Board Clerk shall state “a motion is in order to certify the results of the recount of the 
vote on Question #2 from the November 3, 2026 election.” 
 
  
 ADJOURNMENT 
 
8. This being a special meeting of the board, no further business can be presented unless by 2/3 
majority and a motion is in order to adjourn. 
 
 
 
 
Statement of nondiscrimination: It is the policy of the Manchester Board of School Committee, in its actions, and those of its employees, that there shall 
be no discrimination on the basis of age, sex, race, color, marital status, physical or mental disability, religious creed, national origin or sexual orientation 
for employment in, or operation and administration of any program or activity in the Manchester School District.  The Title IX Coordinator is Dr. Kelly 
Espinola for staff and students. 
 
Per the Strategic Plan, our Mission objective is to provide a transformational learning experience and ensure that every MSD learner has high 
quality postsecondary options to attain a technical certificate, gainful employment, and/or a two-year or four-year degree.

NOTE: Per RSA 32:5-i, VI, "(t)he moderator of each municipality or ward in the school administrative unit shall report  the results on the question to the 
secretary of the school administrative unit board served by the municipality or ward."  Adoption requires a 3/5 majority vote of the voters voting as referenced 
in the above mentioned statute. 
Question 2
Shall the City of MANCHESTER ... limit property tax growth for MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT (SAU #37) under RSA 32:5-i? If 
adopted for a two-year period: (1) the local property tax levy may not grow beyond the prior year’s amount, adjusted for inflation and new 
construction; (2) SAU central office spending may not exceed 6 percent of total school district appropriations; and (3) bonded capital 
costs are excluded from both limits. These caps apply only to administrative operations of the SAU central office and do not affect 
classroom instruction, school-based services, or other municipal expenditures. These limits may be overridden as provided in RSA 32:5-
i. Adoption requires a three-fifths (3/5) majority vote.”


RULES OF PROCEDURES FOR RECOUNTS 
RSA 32:5-i 
 
Recount of Question 2 – November 3, 2026, General Election 
Date: Friday, November 20, 2026 
Time: 8:00 a.m. – until completion 
Location: Welcome Center, 148 Concord Street, Manchester, NH 
 
1. The Board of School Committee, acting as the Board of Recount pursuant to NH RSA 
32:5, shall approve the Procedures for the Recount. 
2. Only Question 2, for which a recount has been requested, shall be recounted. All other 
offices and questions on the ballot will not be recounted. 
3. An office or question may only be recounted once. 
4. After the rules have been approved, the Clerk shall state, “we will now begin the recount 
process.” 
5. The Board of School Committee Clerk shall coordinate the recount process using four 
(4)-person teams.  Each four person team will be made up of two team members who 
shall be responsible for the initial verification of the votes, and two team members who 
shall be responsible for independently tallying the verified ballots. 
6. The petitioners may designate one or two observers for each recount team. If there are 
two observers, one shall be located at the verification table and one shall be located at the 
recount table.   
 
7. The observers shall not converse with the team verifying and counting the votes, except 
to challenge the verification of a specific vote.   
 
8. Only observers whose names have been submitted in advance shall be permitted within 
the designated recount area. All other spectators shall remain outside the recount area 
until the completion of the recount.   
9. No observer shall possess or use a writing instrument or electronic communication device 
while they are within the designated recount area. 
10. Observers shall not touch or otherwise handle any ballots. 
11. All communication devices are to be turned off or turned to silent mode in the recount 
area. All phone conversations are to be conducted outside of the designated recount area.

Page 2 of 3 
 
12. The ballots will be verified and recounted by Ward, beginning with Ward 1.   
13. Ballot boxes will be opened by the Clerk or designated recount supervisor and at the 
completion of the verification and recount process will be sealed by the Clerk or 
designated recount supervisor. 
14. The two team members responsible for the initial verification shall receive the ballots 
cast in the election from the Board Clerk or designated recount supervisor. The team 
members shall verify the votes cast on Question 2. Once verification is completed, the 
ballots shall be transferred to the two team members responsible for recounting and 
tallying the votes. 
15. The two recount team members shall alternate announcing the vote cast on Question 2 for 
each ballot, identifying whether the voter selected "Yes," selected "No," or 
overvoted/undervoted the question. The ballot shall be displayed so that the designated 
observer may view the vote. 
16. The recount team shall place the ballots in clearly designated areas labeled "Yes," "No," 
and “Blank (Undervote and Overvote)." Ballots subject to a challenge shall be removed 
from the recount table and brought to the Board of School Committee for adjudication.  
The recount will continue while the board deliberates on any challenged ballot. 
17. The Vice Chair of the Board of School Committee shall be the spokesman for the Board 
when announcing the results of any challenged votes. 
18. If there is a challenge of any vote, it must be made immediately by the observer. 
Challenged votes shall be ruled upon by the Board of School Committee. Any ballot 
challenged by an observer shall be identified and at that time, the team shall raise their 
hand to relinquish possession of the ballot to the Board Clerk and bring the ballot to the 
Board of School Committee for a ruling. 
19. Once a challenged ballot has been presented to the Board of School Committee for 
determination, the Board shall consider the ballot and render its decision. The Board may 
request clarification as necessary.  At no time will the petitioners or their representatives 
be permitted to engage with the Board of School Committee. 
20. In no case shall rejected absentee, spoiled, cancelled, or ballets voided at the polls on 
Election Day, be considered by the Board of School Committee for a ruling.   
21. In no case shall the Federal Office Only (FOO) ballots be included in the recount.  
22. During the recount, the designated recount supervisor may transfer ballots from the 
clearly marked areas at the recount table to the counting table, maintaining the separation 
and identification of each category of verified ballots.
2026-11-20 – Rules of Procedure – Recount on Question #2 
Page 3 of 3 
 
23. Once all eligible ballots have been reviewed, verified and announced by the recount 
team, the ballots shall be counted and the totals verified by the team assigned to the 
counting table. 
 
24. The Board Clerk shall maintain a recount tally sheet reflecting the votes reported on 
Election Day by the ward election officials and the votes determined upon completion of 
the recount. The tally sheet shall separately identify the total number of "Yes" votes, 
"No" votes, and “blank (undervotes/overvotes)”. 
 
25. Upon completion of the recount, the Board Clerk shall prepare the final recount tally 
sheet and present the verified results to the Board of School Committee, for review and 
approval. 
 
26. The Board of School Committee shall determine and declare the results of Question 2 
based on the verified recount tally sheet. Pursuant to NH RSA 32:5-i, approval of 
Question 2 requires an affirmative vote of at least three-fifths (60%) majority of the 
voters voting  in Manchester.  
27. The petitioners who requested the recount may cancel at any time during the procedure, 
at which time the Board Clerk will publicly announce the petitioners request to cancel the 
recount and the recount will cease at once. 
28. If a recount shows that Question 2 passed, the Board Clerk, within 10 days after such 
recount, shall return the filing fee. 
29. Following the conclusion of the recount, the final results shall be recorded and certified 
as required by applicable law. The recount records, including tally sheets, challenges, 
determinations, and other relevant documentation, shall be preserved in accordance with 
applicable law. 
 
30. Nothing in these procedures shall be construed to limit any right of appeal or judicial 
review otherwise available under applicable law.
